source.title: ImageNet/ResNet-50 Training in 224 Seconds
source.authors: Hiroaki Mikami; Hisahiro Suganuma; Pongsakorn U-chupala; Yoshiki Tanaka; Yuichi Kageyama

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether large-batch training widens the natural-label validation gap and whether batch-size control and label smoothing affect that outcome, using ImageNet/ResNet-50.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own validation-accuracy results for batch-size conditions and techniques. The generalization-gap language in the introduction and cited studies is not counted as this paper's result.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's recipe-adaptation clause through its own ImageNet/ResNet-50 validation results with batch-size control and label smoothing. Table 3 specifies 90-epoch schedules, contrary to the record's claim that fixed-epoch comparisons are absent. All conditions already use large batches and adapted recipes, so they do not establish the unadapted small-versus-large-batch penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: batch-size control and label smoothing separately enable larger batches with little reported accuracy loss, whereas their tested combination reduces accuracy. The authors also emphasize achieving 75.29% validation accuracy in 122 seconds and over 80% GPU scaling efficiency through 2048 GPUs.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet/ResNet-50 distributed-training benchmark; tests batch-size control and label smoothing, with LARS, warmup, mixed precision, and batch normalization without moving average. It does not report matched fixed-epoch small- versus large-batch training.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation accuracy differed across batch-size control, label smoothing, their combination, and the stated configurations; the combined condition had lower accuracy.
record.problems: Validation accuracy is reported, but training error is not, so the generalization gap cannot be directly calculated. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Batch size, number of GPUs, and some training settings vary together across experiments.
record.rows_left_out: None of the paper's own reported validation-accuracy rows for the tested version were omitted. Table 1 values for prior work are cited comparisons, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under controlled tuning.

Unadapted small-versus-large-batch comparisons, the workload-dependent threshold, language models, and recovery through longer training. No same-batch ablation isolates the benefit of each adaptation.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Table 3 supplies a common 90-epoch budget, but the reference batch is already 32K and several settings vary together. No uncertainty estimates or statistical tests substantiate the authors' significance wording. States for R3 and R5 describe absence of the batch penalty; their verdict supports the adaptation clause of V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
The study does not report language models, fixed-epoch matched-batch comparisons, or some cited recipe changes as its own results.
Dropout and its interaction with weight decay or data augmentation.
Sharpness or other measures tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained ImageNet with reference configuration and fixed training schedule.
rows.note: Reference condition; the table reports validation accuracy and time but not training error, so the train-test gap itself cannot be computed.
rows.check: Valid reference accuracy, but this row alone cannot establish a batch-size penalty. Missing training error does not prevent evaluating V5, which concerns held-out performance.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch-size control, increasing the mini-batch from 34K to 68K.
rows.note: Validation accuracy is 0.37 percentage points below the reference; no training-error measurement is reported.
rows.check: Accuracy is 0.37 percentage points below the reference. Exp. 1 also used an earlier software version; recipe and software differences prevent attributing this difference solely to batch size.

source_check.locator_found: Tables 3 and 5; footnote 5 identifies the earlier software version.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with label smoothing and a fixed mini-batch.
rows.note: Authors say label smoothing alone enabled 54K initial mini-batch with no significant accuracy loss.
rows.check: The authors characterize the 0.11-point decrease as no significant accuracy loss, so partial overstates the residual penalty. This absence supports V5's adaptation clause. The batch stays at 54K.

source_check.locator_found: Tables 3 and 5, Exp. 2; Section 3.3 describes no significant accuracy loss.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Combined batch-size control and label smoothing with a changing mini-batch.
rows.note: Authors explicitly report that combining the techniques with large mini-batch size decreases accuracy by about 0.7%.
rows.check: The 0.78-point accuracy decrease is a batch-associated performance penalty, not its reversal. It shows that combining the adaptations does not preserve reference accuracy in this condition.

source_check.locator_found: Tables 3 and 5, Exp. 3; Section 3.3 reports an approximately 0.7% accuracy decrease.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch-size control, increasing the mini-batch from 34K to 119K.
rows.note: Authors say batch-size control alone allowed a maximum mini-batch of 119K with no significant accuracy loss; the reported value is 0.17 percentage points below the reference.
rows.check: The authors characterize the 0.17-point decrease as no significant accuracy loss. The 119K batch is reached late in training; this is not constant-119K training.

source_check.locator_found: Tables 3 and 5, Exp. 4; Section 3.3 describes no significant accuracy loss.

relationships.condition: 90-epoch ImageNet/ResNet-50 training with label smoothing at constant 54K or batch-size control from 34K to 119K
relationships.reason: R3 and R5 reach 75.29% and 75.23% versus the 75.40% reference; the authors describe both losses as insignificant, supporting preservation of accuracy with adapted recipes.
relationships.display_finding: The adapted recipes achieved 75.29% and 75.23% accuracy versus the 75.40% batch-32K reference, without statistical tests establishing equivalence.

tranche.reason: The study tests batch-size control and label smoothing through its own fixed-budget ImageNet/ResNet-50 validation results, bearing on V5's recipe-adaptation clause.
